title: Agent Lifecycle Common Schema
description: ALR-1101 (Agent Lifecycle Record, Part 1): the shared closed-vocabulary definitions for the four orthogonal record axes -- governance, identity, coverage, comparability -- plus the trust-level authority ceiling and the bounded reason-code vocabulary they all draw from. This document is a resolved definitions target: no axis constrains another (each closed type binds its own trust_level/reason_codes independently), unknown/legacy inputs resolve to the least-authority value rather than being echoed, and no client-supplied evidence can ever produce server_verified. The generic AxisValue base is intentionally not referenced by anything else in this file -- it exists only to document the shared shape and to let tests demonstrate why each axis needs its own closed oneOf instead of accepting any value/trust_level/reason_codes combination. The root of this document resolves to AgentLifecycleAxisSet purely as a convenient, uniform validation entry point for this story's corpus; every individual axis definition remains independently $ref-able by future route schemas. Reserved-but-producerless values (identity VERIFIED; governance ADVISORY/STRICT; comparability COMPARABLE/NON_COMPARABLE) are intentionally schema-VALID here -- Part 1 has no route that emits them, which is a producer/service-level guarantee owned by later stories, not a schema-level rejection.

TrustLevel.description: The authority ceiling shared by every axis. client_attested: sourced from client-supplied input, never independently verified. backend_observed: Backend read or derived this from its own persisted state. server_verified: reserved for a canonical Backend-managed verification issuer; structurally legal but has no Part 1 producer. No client-supplied evidence may ever resolve to server_verified.

BoundedReasonCode.description: Closed bounded reason vocabulary for every axis reason_codes array in this file; no free text and no unenumerated codes are legal. The first ten members are pinned by the Part 1 Contract Freeze reason-code inventory. IDENTICAL_MEASUREMENT_CONTRACT_BASIS and REQUIRED_COMPARISON_INPUT_UNKNOWN are ALR-1101 authoring additions for the reserved ComparabilityVerdictAxisValue COMPARABLE/NON_COMPARABLE branches, which the frozen contract structurally reserves (no Part 1 producer) without itself pinning a reason-code tuple for them; this is flagged as a contract gap in the ALR-1101 delivery notes, not treated as a frozen value.

AxisValue.description: Closed structural base requiring exactly value/trust_level/reason_codes; reason_codes is always a unique array, including when empty. Not a public escape hatch: nothing else in this document references this definition directly, and no route schema may either. Every public governance/identity/comparability/coverage property must use its own axis-specific closed definition below, each of which binds trust_level and reason_codes structurally per legal value instead of accepting any combination this generic base alone would allow.

GovernanceProfileAxisValue.description: Closed governance-profile axis. OBSERVED is the only value any Part 1 route ever emits: Backend's DB/server default, ORM default, backfill, and read fallback all yield OBSERVED, and unknown or legacy governance inputs resolve to it rather than being echoed back. ADVISORY and STRICT remain reserved -- structurally legal, always backend_observed with no bound reason -- but authorize no Part 1 action and have no Part 1 response producer.

IdentityStateAxisValue.description: Closed oneOf over the four structurally legal identity tuples. Reserved VERIFIED is exactly server_verified/[REGISTERED_PROVENANCE] but has no Part 1 producer. Live RECONSTRUCTED is exactly client_attested/[DECLARED_PROVENANCE]; historical RECONSTRUCTED is exactly client_attested/[LEGACY_RECONSTRUCTED] -- the historical trust floor is deliberate: the join is Backend-observed but the underlying provenance originated client-side. Live UNKNOWN is exactly client_attested/[REQUIRED_IDENTITY_UNKNOWN] and always retains that reason; it can never become VERIFIED, and no other tuple is legal.

ComparabilityVerdictAxisValue.description: Closed oneOf over the three structurally legal comparability tuples. A single-record read is exactly NOT_APPLICABLE/backend_observed/[SINGLE_SUBJECT] -- Part 1's only actively producible branch. COMPARABLE requires an identical measurement-contract basis between the two records under comparison (bound to IDENTICAL_MEASUREMENT_CONTRACT_BASIS) and NON_COMPARABLE is the mandatory verdict whenever a required comparison input is unknown (bound to REQUIRED_COMPARISON_INPUT_UNKNOWN) -- never a permissive default. Both remain reserved with no Part 1 Route 5 producer; no delta or recommendation is emitted in Part 1.

RecordMeasurementCoverage.description: Closed oneOf between (a) a selected live reconciliation with eight integer counts and basis=LATEST_SEALED_EVIDENCE_EPISODE, (b) a bound private legacy marker with state=UNKNOWN, basis=UNKNOWN_LEGACY_BASIS, all eight counts exactly null, trust_level=client_attested, and reason_codes const [LEGACY_RECONSTRUCTED], and (c) an unmeasured projection with state=UNMEASURED, all eight counts schema-const 0, and basis NO_EVIDENCE_EPISODE|NO_SEALED_EVIDENCE_EPISODE selected from live episode cardinality. Owner accounting decision (2026-08-09, simpler contract): there is no commitment field and no observed_unique field anywhere in this type; duplicate submissions are rejected before acceptance and every accepted count object carries duplicate as schema-const 0 (const null on the legacy-marker branch, alongside the other seven counts). expected/produced/cached/missing/failed/fallback/excluded/duplicate are the complete eight-count set; no ninth accounting field is legal.

AgentLifecycleAxisSet.description: The reusable set of orthogonal axis fields that a Part 1 record composes from this common schema: governance_profile, identity_state, measurement_coverage, comparability_verdict. Each axis validates independently -- no combination of one axis's legal value narrows what another axis may legally hold -- and the closed object rejects any field this set does not name.
